markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (54%)** · Ambiguous: Benign vs Invasive · Careful review
Invasive (45%) sits in the 90% conformal set [F1]; simulated margin call is tumor at margin [F7].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 54%, Invasive 45% | Nearly split |
| Conformal set | Benign, Invasive | Cannot separate classes |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.88 / 62nd percentile | Typical, usable input |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 2/5 Benign [F5] | Mixed neighbors |

## Tissue evidence
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 2, 3, 7) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F2] · Weak
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 8) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; associated with invasive carcinoma [F4] · Validated
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 0, 4, 9) · ↑ invasive · Above typical, but spot check only 3/20 · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Concept deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007); not shown to reflect the classifier. Necrosis is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Neighbors are split (2 Benign, 2 Invasive, 1 InSitu), so the Benign call is weakly supported.
- Regions 0, 1, 4, 5, 8, 9 each lean strongly invasive; the other six pull toward Benign.

## Check on the slide
1. **8** — Confirm tumor-infiltrating stroma; it is a validated invasive cue (19/20).
2. **0, 4, 9** — Verify necrosis directly; its AI spot check failed (3/20).
3. **2, 3, 7** — Confirm glands are benign, not invasive tubule formation.
